sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Founded 1488 by Rao Bikaji, a Rathore prince and one of Rao Jodhaji's (founder of Jodhpur) five sons, after leaving his father's court and settling the wilderness called Jangladesh. Nicknamed 'Camel Country'; holds one of only two surviving WWI British biplanes gifted to Maharaja Ganga Singh; sand dunes scattered through the district, mainly northeast to south.

places.name: Junagarh Fort
places.facts: Built 1588 AD by Raja Rai Singh, a general of Emperor Akbar; never captured in its history; red sandstone and marble palaces with courtyards, balconies, kiosks, windows.

places.name: National Research Centre on Camel
places.facts: Only camel research/breeding centre of its kind in Asia; spread over 2000 acres, managed by the Government of India; camel rides, selfie points, camel milk products (flavored milk, coffee, kulfi, cheese).

places.name: Lalgarh Palace and Museum
places.facts: Commissioned by Maharaja Ganga Singh, built 1902 in memory of his father Maharaja Lal Singh; entirely red sandstone; designed by Sir Swinton Jacob blending Rajputana, Islamic, and European styles.

places.name: Rampuria Haveli (Rampuria Group of Havelis)
places.facts: Built of dulmera (red) stone; ornate jharokhas, latticed windows, divankhanas, gumaharias (basements); gold work, Victorian-influenced design, exquisite wood carving.

places.name: Ganga Government Museum
places.facts: Described as the state's best museum; Harappan and early Gupta period archaeological artefacts; separate sections for paintings, arts/crafts, woven carpets, clay pottery, ancient coins, Rajput weaponry.

places.name: Laxmi Niwas Palace
places.facts: Residence of Maharaja Ganga Singh, built 1898-1902 by British architect Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob; Indo-Saracenic style; now a luxury hotel.

places.name: Prachina Museum
places.facts: Royal costumes, textiles, accessories; 'Poshaks' (ladies' garments) showing traditional craft; royal family portraits.

places.name: Deshnok Karni Mata Temple
places.facts: Stone and marble temple; Karni Mata idol decorated with mukut (tiara) and garlands, flanked by images of her sisters and Avad Mata's sisters; world-famous for kabas (rats) roaming freely in the temple precincts.

places.name: Jain Temple Bhandasar
places.facts: 15th-century temple dedicated to the 5th Tirthankar, Sumatinathji; one of Bikaner's oldest monuments; intricate mirror work, murals, gold leaf paintings.

places.name: Kodamdesar Temple and Lake
places.facts: Kodamdesar Bhainru Ji installed by Rao Bikaji shortly after arriving from Jodhpur; originally chosen as Bikaner's foundation site before relocation; lake in the temple's backyard.

places.name: Shri Laxminath Temple
places.facts: Marble and red stone; Bikaner's rulers regarded Lord Laxminathji (Vishnu) as the true king, considering themselves his Diwans/Ministers; enshrines his throne.

places.name: Shiv Bari Temple (Laleshwar Mahadev Mandir)
places.facts: Built by Maharaja Doongar Singh in the 19th century in memory of his father Maharaja Lal Singh; four-faced black marble Shiva statue, bronze Nandi; wall paintings; two large bawari reservoirs.

places.name: Gajner Palace and Lake
places.facts: Founded 1784 by Maharaja Gaj Singh, completed by Maharaja Ganga Singh on the lake's banks; former royal hunting/relaxation lodge; now a heritage hotel.

places.name: Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary
places.facts: Nilgai, chinkara, blackbuck, wild boar; imperial sand grouse flocks and migratory winter birds.

places.name: Devi Kund
places.facts: Royal crematorium of the Bikaji dynasty; chhatris marking cremation sites of rulers; Maharaja Surat Singh's white marble chhatri with Rajput ceiling paintings notable; also cenotaphs of 22 royal women who committed sati, plus one male sati (sata) cenotaph.

places.name: Rajasthan State Archives
places.facts: Mughal-period Persian Farmans, Nishans, Manshurs; princely-state administrative records; newly developed museum gallery.

places.name: Kolayat
places.facts: Hindu pilgrimage town; associated with sage Kapil Muni (Sankhya yoga), said to have paused his journey here for tapasya; temples, ghats, a sacred lake, and town market.

places.name: Katariasar Village
places.facts: Rural desert village with sand dunes and sunset views; home to the Jasnathjis, known fire dancers; chinkara, desert fox, rabbit, peacock, parrot, partridge sightings.

places.name: Jorbeed
places.facts: One of Asia's largest congregations of eagles and vultures; Steppe Eagles, Griffon Vultures, Egyptian Vultures common; rare yellow-eyed pigeon possible.

places.name: Horse Ecotourism (National Research Centre on Equines, Bikaner Campus)
places.facts: Horse/pony/tonga/buggy riding; Marwari, Kathiawari, Zanskari, Manipuri horses plus French Poitou and White Gujarati donkeys; Equine Information Centre; hydrotherapy pool for equines; handicraft/leather souvenir shops.

places.name: Darbari Lake
places.facts: Popular monsoon-season picnic spot; favoured by trekkers; lush green catchment area.

places.name: Raisar Dunes
places.location: 18 km from Bikaner, Bikaner-Jaipur highway, Raisar village
places.facts: Desert safari, camel safari, camel-cart ride, jeep safari, night camping; compared in scale to Jaisalmer's Sam Sand Dunes.

places.name: Public Park
places.facts: Built 1937 to mark Maharaja Ganga Singh's reign; modeled as a replica of Buckingham Palace Garden in Westminster.

places.name: Karni Mata Panorama
places.location: Near Nehdi Ji (old Karni Mata temple), Bikaner
places.facts: Panorama depicting Karni Mata's life and deeds; features an ashtadhatu (eight-metal alloy) statue of the goddess.

howToReach.air: Nal Airport, ~10 km from Bikaner, direct connectivity from Delhi and Jaipur
howToReach.rail: Connections to Jaipur, Jaisalmer, Churu, Jodhpur, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Guwahati
howToReach.road: Frequent express buses to Agra, Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Barmer, Delhi, Jaipur, Jaisalmer, Jhunjhunu, Jodhpur, Kota, Udaipur
